claims.text: Defense Intelligence Reference Document titled "Aneutronic Fusion Propulsion", series "Defense Futures", published 2010-11-01 with an Intelligence Cut-Off Date (ICOD) of 2010-07-20, DIA document number DIA-08-1011-003. Released by DIA under FOIA and posted in the DIA FOIA Electronic Reading Room.

Inside cover reads: "This product is one in a series of advanced technology reports produced in FY 2009 under the Defense Intelligence Agency [redacted b(3) 10 USC 424] Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications (AAWSA) Program" and directs questions to the "AAWSA Program Manager, Defense Intelligence Agency, ATTN: [redacted], Bldg 6000, Washington, DC 20340-5100".

Author name is withheld in the DIA-released copy under FOIA exemption (b)(6); the "Prepared by:" line is withheld under (b)(3) 10 USC 424. The released cover therefore does not attribute the DIRD to a named author.
Released PDF is 50 pages, marked UNCLASSIFIED//FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY (FOUO caveat partially illegible in the scan).

The DIA list of 9 January 2018 records TWO distinct aneutronic fusion deliverables, not one: item 26 "Aneutronic Fusion Propulsion, Dr V Teofilo, Lockheed Martin" and item 30 "Aneutronic Fusion Propulsion II, Dr W Culbreth, Univ of Nevada-Las Vegas". The apparent duplication on the board is therefore genuine bibliography, not a data error.

Cover page reads "01 November 2010 / ICOD: 20 July 2010 / DIA-08-1011-003", series "Defense Futures" (not "Acquisition Threat Support"), with a singular "Author:" field redacted under (b)(6). The document runs 50 pages with 28 endnotes.

Assigned to Culbreth by elimination and by internal character: this document contains five separate Nevada Test Site passages (Project Rover, NERVA at Area 25, Silverpeak lithium mining), cites standard nuclear engineering textbooks, and includes a relativistic rocket worksheet appendix, while containing zero occurrences of "Lockheed", "Teofilo", "Sunnyvale" or any Lockheed Martin content. The companion document DIA-08-1011-004 does contain a V. Teofilo self-citation. Neither cover names its author.

connections.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
connections.note: Tier 2, and the reason is worth stating. A full-text scan of this released DIRD on 23 August 2026 found NO occurrence of the programme name anywhere in the document - unlike 27 of the 32 scanned, whose inside cover names the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program explicitly. The link therefore rests on the DIA's 9 January 2018 list to the Senate Armed Services Committee, which enumerates it among the 38 reference products, and not on the document's own text.

connections.label: William Culbreth
connections.note: TIER 2 AND DELIBERATELY SO. The DIA list establishes at tier 1 that two aneutronic fusion DIRDs exist, one by V. Teofilo (Lockheed Martin) and one by W. Culbreth (UNLV). Which released document number belongs to which author is NOT stated on either cover, both of which redact the author under (b)(6). This document, DIA-08-1011-003, is assigned to Culbreth because the companion DIA-08-1011-004 carries a V. Teofilo self-citation at endnote 17 and Lockheed Martin content, while this one carries none of either and is instead saturated with Nevada Test Site, Project Rover and NERVA material plus nuclear engineering textbook citations. If the mapping is ever shown to be reversed, this edge and its partner must be swapped together.
